summary:
MISSION27 is an interactive 3D lunar mission simulator designed to help young learners aged 7–12 and beyond experience the challenges astronauts face.
Inspired by real space exploration experiences, we created a game where players first train on Earth to understand life support, radiation, power management, and other essential skills. They then apply what they've learned during a simulated 27-hour lunar mission, exploring the Moon, driving rovers, collecting samples, resolving crew conflicts, and responding to unexpected emergencies such as crop stress, spacesuit cooling failures, power outages, air leaks and many more with  different tasks.
By incorporating real NASA scientific data and research into interactive activities, MISSION27 turns complex space science into something young explorers can experience for themselves.
Our goal is to make astronaut training more accessible, engaging, and meaningful while encouraging curiosity, critical thinking, and teamwork.
details:
MISSION27 – Train on Earth. Survive the Moon.

Space exploration has always fascinated us, but we realized that understanding what astronauts actually experience takes more than reading textbooks or watching videos. Astronauts must manage limited resources, operate complex systems, respond to unexpected emergencies, and work together under challenging conditions. Inspired by real astronaut experiences, including Eugene Cernan's difficult spacewalk during Gemini IX-A in 1966, we wanted to create something that would allow young learners to experience these challenges in a safe and interactive environment.

This idea became MISSION27, an interactive, browser-based 3D lunar mission simulator developed for NASA's Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge.

How MISSION27 Works

Our game follows a training-first approach, divided into two connected stages: Earth Training and Lunar Mission.

In Earth Training, players learn essential astronaut skills through interactive activities covering life-support systems, radiation safety, power management, solar energy, space agriculture, equipment maintenance, and EVA preparation. Instead of simply reading instructions, they interact with different systems, make decisions, and understand how those decisions affect mission operations.

Once their training is complete, players begin a simulated 27-hour lunar mission, where they apply their knowledge in a 360-degree, explorable Moon environment.

Throughout the mission, players complete 16 objectives involving lunar rover exploration, scientific sample collection, Earth photography, resource management, and crew cooperation. They also encounter unexpected situations, including solar particle events, air leaks, spacesuit cooling failures, power outages, and greenhouse crop stress.

One feature we particularly wanted to include was crew conflict. Space missions are not only about technology; communication, cooperation, and decision-making are equally important. Through simulated disagreements and teamwork challenges, players learn that a successful mission depends on how people work together.

Integration of NASA Scientific Data

A major part of MISSION27 is connecting gameplay with authentic NASA scientific resources.

We incorporated information from NASA JPL Horizons for solar-position calculations, RadLab for historical space radiation measurements, OSDR studies for space agriculture, LOLA for lunar terrain references, DONKI for historical space-weather events, and EPIC for Earth observation imagery.

These resources help transform scientific concepts into interactive educational activities. For example, players can explore solar-energy decisions using NASA-calculated Sun positions, examine radiation measurements, and investigate plant-growing conditions based on space agriculture research.

The scientific references and selected measurements come from real NASA resources, while mission scenarios, resource changes, and gameplay outcomes are simulated for educational purposes.

Technology and Development

MISSION27 was developed as a web application using React, TypeScript, Three.js, React Three Fiber, and supporting frontend technologies.

We used Lovable for AI-assisted development of the 3D environment, interactive systems, user interface, and gameplay mechanics. ChatGPT supported our research organization, brainstorming, technical problem-solving, debugging, and documentation.

Our five-member team, CREW-M27, guided the project's concept, selected scientific resources, designed the educational activities, tested the game, identified technical problems, and directed improvements throughout development.

The game runs in a web browser, making it easier to access without specialized hardware. We also considered responsive design, navigation, readable instructions, and age-appropriate interactions for our primary audience of learners aged 7–12 and beyond.

Creativity and Intended Impact

What makes MISSION27 different is the connection between preparation and experience. Players do not simply arrive on the Moon and begin completing tasks. They first learn essential skills on Earth and then discover why those skills matter when facing lunar mission challenges.

We wanted to combine scientific authenticity with engaging gameplay, allowing young learners to explore complicated topics without requiring advanced technical knowledge.

Our team considered educational value, accessibility, scientific accuracy, user experience, problem-solving, teamwork, and the importance of making mistakes in a safe simulated environment.

Ultimately, our goal is not just to teach children facts about space. We want to encourage curiosity, build confidence, strengthen critical thinking, and inspire the next generation to explore science, engineering, and technology.

We believe the lessons learned during training on Earth can help prepare tomorrow's explorers for the challenges of the Moon.

This is MISSION27.
